purpose: Mandatory architecture and security addendum to XPEX-CONTENT-002.codex.json. Codex must satisfy both files before requesting review.

facts: Course creation enforces resource CREATE authorization plus explicit organization membership and creates the authenticated actor as ResourceAuthor.
Course creation commits Course and ResourceAuthor atomically inside its own transaction.
Chapter creation authorizes against the parent course and commits Chapter plus CourseChapter inside its own transaction.
Activity creation authorizes against the parent course and commits Activity plus ChapterActivity inside its own transaction.
Native course update can mutate published through the generic UPDATE path; the additional sensitive-field validation currently enumerates public and open_to_contributors, not published.
Core elevated organization roles are ADMIN=1 and MAINTAINER=2.
Because native course/chapter/activity create services each commit independently, composing them naively is not an all-or-nothing multi-entity publication transaction.

editorial_persistence: Persist AI editorial drafts separately from native LearnHouse Course/Chapter/Activity rows until the explicit Publish action.
Editorial persistence is workflow metadata/content staging only; it must not implement enrollment, progress, completion, certification, learner access, or a parallel LMS.
Every draft must have immutable draft_id, org_id/org_uuid scope, revision integer, content_hash, schema_version, created_by, created_at and updated_at.
state_and_revision_binding: Allowed states remain DRAFT, REVIEWED, APPROVED, PUBLISHED.
Review evidence must bind to the exact revision and content_hash reviewed.
Approval evidence must bind to the exact revision and content_hash approved.
Any content-bearing edit increments revision, recalculates content_hash and invalidates prior review and approval evidence.
Publish must compare current revision/hash with approved revision/hash server-side and reject stale approval with 409 or equivalent fail-closed response.
approval_evidence: Store approver actor UUID/user ID, organization scope, timestamp, approved revision, approved content_hash and authorization decision context.
Never accept approved_by, approved_at, approved revision/hash, PUBLISHED status, or native identifiers from client-controlled mass assignment.
Re-authorize the authenticated actor server-side at both Approve and Publish; authentication at page load is not sufficient.
publish_boundary: No native LearnHouse Course/Chapter/Activity row may be created by Generate, Review, Edit or Approve.
Only the explicit authorized Publish action may cross the boundary from editorial draft storage into native LearnHouse records.

Create the native Course initially with published=false, build all required chapters/activities, verify the complete authoritative mapping, and only then perform the final explicit native published=true transition.
Do not expose a partially built course publicly.
Do not rely on a browser-supplied published flag.
authorization: Reuse native LearnHouse RBAC and organization membership; do not invent a second auth system.
Generate/Review/Edit access must be explicitly defined from existing roles/permissions.

Approve and Publish require elevated server-side authorization. Unless a stronger existing permission primitive is discovered, restrict Approve and Publish to ADMIN or MAINTAINER and document the exact reused primitive.
Every draft lookup/mutation must include organization scoping to prevent cross-org IDOR.
API-token behavior must be explicitly decided and tested; do not accidentally inherit browser/editor permissions for API tokens.
idempotency_and_concurrency: Publish must accept or derive a stable idempotency key tied to draft_id plus approved revision/hash.
Two concurrent Publish requests for the same approved revision must produce one native course, never duplicates.
Use database uniqueness/locking or an equivalent durable server-side mechanism; an in-memory lock is insufficient.
Edit/Review/Approve/Publish mutations must reject stale revision writes using optimistic concurrency or equivalent compare-and-swap semantics.
partial_failure_strategy: Native create services commit independently, so the publisher must implement a deliberate partial-failure strategy rather than claiming cross-service atomicity.
Preferred behavior: keep the native course unpublished until every chapter/activity is created and verified.

On failure before final publication, record FAILED/RECOVERABLE publication attempt metadata and either compensate by deleting only the publisher-created unpublished native tree or allow deterministic resume using persisted native IDs.
Never delete or overwrite a pre-existing native resource during compensation.
A retry must resume or safely converge without creating duplicate chapters/activities.
native_mapping: Persist the authoritative mapping from editorial draft/revision to native course_uuid/course_id, chapter IDs/UUIDs and activity IDs/UUIDs.
After success, PUBLISHED is terminal for that approved revision and returns the canonical native destination.
The mapping must be auditable and sufficient to prove which exact approved content produced which native records.
security_and_observability: Provider tokens, Authorization headers, Railway variable values and raw provider error bodies must never be logged or returned.
Treat generated, reviewed and stored course text as untrusted data at every provider/UI boundary.
Structured logs may include draft_id, org_id, revision, hash prefix, actor UUID, transition, provider/model name, sanitized result and native IDs after publication.
Do not log full generated course bodies by default in production.
Apply bounded module_count/body sizes and provider timeouts already compatible with CONTENT-001; reject abuse fail-closed.

state_integrity: edit after REVIEWED resets/invalidate review evidence
edit after APPROVED resets/invalidate approval evidence
publish with stale approved hash/revision is rejected
client cannot mass-assign APPROVED or PUBLISHED
authorization_and_tenancy: anonymous rejected from all editorial mutations
ordinary learner rejected from protected editorial mutations
API-token path is explicitly allowed with equivalent authorization or explicitly rejected
publish_safety: no native course exists before explicit Publish
native Course begins unpublished during assembly
public visibility remains false until assembly succeeds
concurrent duplicate Publish produces exactly one native course
retry after partial chapter/activity failure converges without duplicates
failed publication never exposes a partial public course
successful publication persists complete editorial-to-native mapping
learner enrollment/progress/completion/certification counts and rows remain unchanged
security: provider secrets absent from frontend bundle and serialized API responses
provider error sanitization does not leak response body/token
stored prompt-injection text cannot alter server workflow state

sequence: Generate one real module with OpenRouter into editorial DRAFT only
Verify zero native LearnHouse Course rows were created by Generate
Run real Hugging Face review and verify REVIEWED only
Verify zero native LearnHouse Course rows were created by Review
Approve explicitly as an authorized human actor and capture approved revision/hash evidence
Verify zero native LearnHouse Course rows were created by Approve
Publish explicitly as an authorized human actor
Verify exactly one native course plus expected chapter/activity tree and authoritative IDs
Verify the final native course is published only after tree assembly
Verify retrying the same publish request does not duplicate the native tree
mandatory_live_smoke.cleanup: The live smoke must use a clearly named test artifact. After evidence capture, either keep it intentionally unpublished/identified as a test fixture or remove it through the native authorized delete path. Never leave accidental public test content.

keep_pr_draft_until: all mandatory tests above are green
migration dry-run green if editorial persistence adds schema
forbidden: native resource creation before explicit Publish
claiming multi-entity atomicity while calling independently committing native services without a verified transaction strategy
